tagline: Self-hosted music streaming server for your own audio files, compatible with Subsonic apps.
description: Navidrome serves a music library you already own to any browser or phone. It reads your files and their tags, watches the folder for changes, and streams in any format, with on-the-fly transcoding that can be set per user or player. It speaks the Subsonic API, so many third-party mobile and desktop clients work with it. It is written in Go and ships as ready-made binaries for macOS, Linux and Windows, plus Docker images for amd64 and arm. The Docker setup needs a data folder it can write to and a music folder it only reads. The docs say it runs on a Raspberry Pi Zero. Each user gets separate play counts, playlists and favourites, and you can scrobble to Last.fm and ListenBrainz. It is the closest self-hosted match to Spotify's player, but it has no catalogue: you bring the files. Managed hosting is offered through partner providers. The licence is GPL-3.0.
strengths: Streams any audio format and transcodes on the fly, with settings per user or player
Works with Subsonic, Madsonic and Airsonic clients, so phone apps already exist
Multi-user, with separate play counts, playlists and favourites for each person
Smart playlists, .m3u import, public share links and scrobbling to Last.fm and ListenBrainz
Official binaries and Docker images for amd64, arm/v6, arm/v7 and arm64
limits: No music catalogue: you must own and organise the audio files yourself
Folder browsing is simulated from tags as /AlbumArtist/Album/Song, so a messy tag set gives a messy library
The master branch can be unstable; the README tells you to install from releases
Playback quality in mobile apps depends on third-party Subsonic clients, not on the project's own apps
bestFor: A listener with a large local music collection and a small server or Raspberry Pi who wants to drop Spotify.
